meta.title: The philosopher who lived in a barrel and mocked a king

plates.want: Gérôme, Diogenes in his jar with his dogs (PD)

plates.query: Diogenes and Alexander the Great painting

beats.text: Diogenes owned a cloak, a stick, and a cup — until he saw a boy drink from his hands.
He threw the cup away. Even that, he decided, was more than a man truly needs.
He slept in a large clay jar and begged for food, free of everything the city chased.
Then Alexander the Great, master of the known world, came to meet him, and offered any gift.
Diogenes looked up and said only: "Stand out of my light."
The most powerful man alive had nothing Diogenes wanted. That was the whole lesson.
Wealth isn't having much. It's needing little — and he was free in a way kings never are.
